summary: We developed "Last Signal", an interactive web application built with React and TypeScript that transforms cold NASA technical logs into an engaging educational experience. The platform features 3D interactive celestial spheres representing the Moon and Mars, allowing users to explore 9 historical rovers, landers, and discarded equipment left behind during space missions. This proyect gives visibility to the equipment left behind and preserves historic milestones for modern space exploration.
details:
Last Signal is an educational web app about the machines humanity left behind on the Moon and Mars. Students explore a 3D Moon and Mars, tap glowing points to meet nine abandoned landers and rovers (Apollo 11, Opportunity, Viking 1 and others), and see a live clock of how long each has been silent. Each machine has a dossier with its story, real NASA photo, sources, and a 3D globe.

Benefit and impact: it turns space history into something students can explore, so they learn that these missions still matter after the signal ends.

Tools: React, TypeScript, Vite and three.js, packaged as a desktop app (Mac/Windows) with Electron. It has no server. Data comes from NASA: LRO maps (LROC, LOLA), the Viking mosaic, NASA photo archives, and NSSDCA records.

Creativity: worlds floating in space, and a “time since last signal” clock for each machine.

Our team’s considerations: accuracy (a teammate approves every entry, with at least two sources each), credit to NASA imagery, and an experience that works in a live demo. We used AI tools to help build the code.
